title: SaaS reference architecture (control plane and data plane)
hook: SaaS reference architecture splits control plane (onboarding, billing, tenant management) from data plane (tenant-facing application logic). The control plane provisions and configures tenant resources; the data plane serves end-user traffic.

blocks.text: Control plane: tenant signup, tier assignment, provisioning Step Functions, billing integration, admin API. Data plane: multi-tenant application serving customer users — APIs, UI, background jobs. AWS patterns: control plane in management account or shared services; data plane pooled ECS/Lambda with tenant context; silo resources vended by control plane workflows. SaaS Lens and AWS SaaS Factory reference architectures document this split.

blocks.text: Senior architects draw two boxes: control plane and data plane. Interviewers ask how onboarding a new tenant works end-to-end. Confusing the two leads to provisioning logic in request hot path.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: control plane manages tenants; data plane serves users; provisioning is async workflow not sync API call.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Tenant signs up
items.body: Control plane API creates tenant record, assigns tier, enqueues provisioning.

items.title: Provision resources
items.body: Step Functions: Cognito app client, schema/DB, usage plan, DNS record.

items.title: Activate tenant
items.body: Status ACTIVE — data plane accepts traffic for tenant_id.

items.title: Serve users
items.body: Data plane routes requests with tenant context; control plane not in hot path.

snippet.label: Step Functions tenant provisioning
snippet.code:
ProvisionTenant:
  Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
  Properties:
    Definition:
      StartAt: CreateTenantRecord
      States:
        CreateTenantRecord:
          Type: Task
          Resource: arn:aws:lambda:...:create-tenant
          Next: ProvisionResources
        ProvisionResources:
          Type: Parallel
          Branches:
            - StartAt: CreateSchema
            - StartAt: CreateCognitoClient
          Next: ActivateTenant
        ActivateTenant:
          Type: Task
          Resource: arn:aws:lambda:...:activate-tenant
          End: true
snippet.explanation: Async provisioning — signup API returns fast, workflow completes in background.

snippet.label: Control plane signup API
snippet.explanation: Never block signup on full provisioning — return status and poll.

snippet.label: Data plane guards tenant status
snippet.explanation: Data plane rejects traffic until control plane marks tenant ACTIVE.

snippet.label: EventBridge tenant lifecycle events
snippet.code:
TenantCreatedRule:
  Type: AWS::Events::Rule
  Properties:
    EventPattern:
      source: [saas.controlplane]
      detail-type: [TenantActivated]
    Targets:
      - Arn: !GetAtt WelcomeEmailLambda.Arn
        Id: WelcomeEmail
snippet.explanation: Decouple control plane events from data plane side effects.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Provisioning in synchronous signup request — timeout and poor UX. Control plane logic in every data plane request path. No tenant status gate — traffic hits half-provisioned tenant.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: p99 signup-to-ACTIVE < 5 min; control plane error rate separate from data plane SLO; provisioning workflow idempotent on retry.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Monolith mixing signup admin and user API with no plane separation — rejected at senior level. Strong answer: control plane provisions async; data plane serves with tenant gate.

interviewTakeaways: Control plane = tenant lifecycle; data plane = end-user traffic.
Provision async via Step Functions — never block signup.
Data plane checks tenant ACTIVE before serving.
60s: CP handles signup, billing, provisioning workflow. DP serves users with tenant context. EventBridge for lifecycle. SaaS Lens reference architecture.
Follow-up: how offboard tenant and delete data?
commonPitfalls: Sync provisioning on signup — timeouts and failures block user.
Strong answer: async workflow, PROVISIONING status, poll until ACTIVE.
No idempotent provisioning — retry creates duplicate resources.
Control plane in data plane hot path — coupling and scale issues.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Separate Express routers for /admin (control) and /api (data) mirror plane split.
TenantActivated event decouples provisioning completion from welcome email — EventBridge pattern locally.
